chunks: And that is that two men in Kūfah, from among the Muslims— a man came to Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام and testified that he had seen them praying to an idol. So ʿAlī عليه السلام said: “Woe to you, perhaps it is someone among those whose matter is confused to you.”

Then he sent a man, and he looked at them while they were praying to an idol, so he brought them. He said: so he said to them, “Return,” but they refused. So he dug for them a trench in the ground, kindled a fire in it, and cast them into it.
Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated that from al-Fuḍayl, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام
key_terms.أُخْدُودًا: a trench dug in the ground
key_terms.ارْجِعَا: return, i.e. go back from disbelief
key_terms.عَنِ: from, indicating transmission in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.يُصَلِّيَانِ: they were performing prayer or worship

ai.seo_question: How did Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام deal with verified apostasy in this narration?
ai.summary: This report narrates that Amīr al-Muʾminīn ʿAlī عليه السلام did not act on a single accusation without verification, but instead sent someone to confirm the matter. After the two men were found praying to an idol and refused to return, he carried out a severe punishment, making the report relevant to the legal discussion of apostasy.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.3551 - And it is reported that two men in Kufa, who were Muslims, were brought before Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as). A man testified that he had seen them praying to an idol.
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Woe unto you! Perhaps it is someone who merely appeared similar to them, and the matter has confused you."

Then, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) sent a man to observe them. The man returned and confirmed that they were indeed praying to an idol.
So, Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) summoned them and said: "Repent and return (to Islam)."
But they refused.
Then, Imam (as) dug a trench in the ground, lit a fire in it, and threw them into the fire.
This was narrated by Musa ibn Bakr from al-Fudayl, from Abu Abdullah (as).
